experiment: Dims: truncation / renormalisation / centring of stored gemma vectors

controls.note: same 35 rows, same query vectors; 256 dims selected WITHOUT the labels

verdict: Truncation to 256-d genuinely improves ranking depth: mean gold rank 2.40 vs 3.00 (or 3.995 for a random 256-dim subset, p=0.003), so the first 256 MRL dimensions are not a random projection. But top-1 (21 vs 19) and top-5 (32 vs 30) gains are not distinguishable from random 256-dim subsets (p=0.23 and 0.025 post-hoc), and every top-1 gain is a fiction row. Centring is worse than baseline on top-5 and mean rank. Verdict: free ordering depth, no reliable free rank-1 or window accuracy.
